LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts . Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot. The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline. Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Follow the game live here Where to watch Texans vs. Colts live Date: Thursday, Nov. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: NRG Stadium (Houston) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Texans -12.5, O/U 44.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Colts have the ball The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces. Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing. Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL . Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions. The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin , Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games. The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor 's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan , including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up. Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state. When the Texans have the ball C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season. The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner , either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins. It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence. This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense. I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Indianapolis traded away several key players at the deadline, including Josh Downs, Keenan Allen, DeForest Buckner, and Quenton Nelson, as the team simply doesn't have the same juice that it did to open the 2025 campaign. Despite that, the Colts have a win over Houston in 2026, and the Texans have struggled against just about everyone this season. Houston is 3-6 through nine games, losing on the road against the Cleveland Browns in Week 10. The Texans blew a 17-0 lead in that matchup, struggling mightily on offense in the second half. While C.J. Stroud has played well in the 2026 season, the Houston defense has not lived up to expectations after it finished No. 1 in EPA/Play during the 2025 campaign. Oddsmakers still have the Texans favored by 12.5 points at home in this AFC South battle. Can Houston get back on track and keep its slim playoff hopes alive? A win on Thursday would go a long way to getting the Texans back in the mix for the No. 7 seed in the AFC. All week long, the SI Betting team shared their favorite picks, player props and predictions for this AFC South matchup. Here's a breakdown of some of our favorites to get you ready to bet on the first primetime matchup in Week 11 of the NFL season. For Thursday Night Football in Week 11, he’s taking the OVER between these AFC South teams: With the spread in the double digits, I have no interest in backing either team. Instead, I'm going to take the OVER. The Texans' offense has been their strength this season. They're now ninth in the league in EPA per play and fourth in that metric since Week 4. C.J. Stroud has also been phenomenal, ranking inside the top eight in almost every quarterback metric since Week 4. Now they'll get to feast against a horrific Colts defense that's 21st in opponent EPA per play. Of course, it's hard to trust the Colts' offense, but it's time for us to continue to assume that the Houston offense is going to turn things around and become the elite unit it was the past few seasons. The biggest red flag in this game is that they're 22nd in opponent rush EPA and 27th in opponent rush success rate, which will feed directly into the Colts' offensive strength with Jonathan Taylor. Jonathan Taylor has seen his snap share dip a bit in recent weeks – playing less than 70 percent of the offensive plays in four games in a row – yet he’s still handled a ton of touches for Indy. Taylor carried the ball 13 times for 46 yards in Week 9 against Dallas and 16 times for 83 yards in Week 10 against Miami. He had 23 carries and cleared this prop in Week 3 against Houston, which is 20th in EPA/Rush and allowing 4.0 yards per carry this season. The Colts star has at least 50 rushing yards in seven of his 10 games this season, picking up at least 45 rushing yards in nine of his games. Taylor is still the safest bet to go off for an Indy team that moved on from both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the trade deadline. Houston wideout Nico Collins has found the end zone in back-to-back weeks, and he has five touchdowns in seven appearances in the 2026 season. In Week 9, Dell had four grabs for 105 yards and a score, receiving nine targets from Stroud. He then followed that up with a three-catch game (on four targets) against Cleveland. Dell isn’t going to lead this receiver room in snaps, but he’s getting looks from Stroud when he’s out there and is now facing a defense that is 18th in EPA/Pass, allowing the sixth-most passing yards in the league. Could the Texans magically turn a corner in this game and look like a more disciplined, refined unit to limit the penalties? It's always possible. (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Texans vs. Browns in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE The Cleveland Browns will get their starting quarterback back in action in Week 10 against the Houston Texans, as Deshaun Watson is off the injury report and set to start. Watson (concussion) missed the team's Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints, though backup Shedeur Sanders played pretty decently in his place. Sanders helped get the Browns to overtime, where they lost on a two-point attempt. The second-year quarterback finished the day with 297 passing yards and two scores, carrying the ball for 28 yards on 10 attempts as well. Still, Todd Monken named Watson the starter for Week 10, as the veteran has led the team to a 5-3 record in eight starts with five fourth quarter comeback wins. In the 2026 season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven scores and three interceptions. He's also carried the ball 51 times for 217 yards and a score. He's playing a revenge game against his former team -- Houston -- in Week 10. Even with Watson back, oddsmakers aren't buying the 5-4 Browns in this matchup. They are 4.5-point underdogs at home in the latest odds at DraftKings , even though they have a better record than an underachieving Houston team so far in 2026. Watson is looking to have a big game to keep the starting job, as it's possible the Browns could turn back to Sanders if things go south. Cleveland is still in the playoff picture in the AFC, but it has taken a step back with two straight losses to Pittsburgh and New Orleans. More importantly, it showed Americans that television cartoons can be relished by adults. So I'm hoping you'll catch my meaning when I use a famous Simpsons quote to personify the Buffalo Bills . The NFL team that famously lost four straight Super Bowls in the 1990s is enjoying a Milhouse moment right now. Milhouse Van Houten is Bart Simpson's lovably awkward and loyal best friend. To co-opt a famous Simpsons quote, "everything's comin' up Milhouse" for the 8-1 Bills, who own the best record in the AFC halfway through the regular season. With the hapless Jets in the rearview mirror and the awful Dolphins coming to town, it's a great time for Bills fans to enjoy the AFC's best record at the season's halfway point. Miami, 1-8 this season, faces a tough battle against the Bills, who are 8-1 this year and currently in position to claim the top spot in the AFC playoff picture. Miami will also be starting quarterback Kyle McCord for just the second time in his career as he continues to fill in for the injured Malik Willis. The injury concerns do not end there, however, as Miami has seen three defensive tackles, Zach Sieler, Zeek Biggers, and Jordan Phillips, land on the injured reserve over the past week. On the first injury report of the week, the Dolphins were without center Aaron Brewer (concussion), punter Bradley Pinion (right groin), cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee), safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad), continuing the injury issues the team is currently battling through. Scheduled to release today, GTA VI is set in a fictionalized version of Miami called Vice City and features a local football team, the Manatees, whose primary colors are aqua and pink. While the Dolphins have not broken out a "Vice City" jersey combination like the Miami Heat have, they are still partnering with Rockstar Games, the game's developers, to ensure the game is represented in Hard Rock Stadium. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Miami Dolphins (1-8) head to Highmark Stadium on Sunday looking to crawl out of the cellar in the AFC East. Their opponent, the Buffalo Bills (8-1) will be looking to maintain their hold on not only the top spot in the division, but in all the AFC. The Bills have won five in a row and are off to their best start since 1991 while the Dolphins are in full tear down so we can rebuild mode. The contrast is especially sharp offensively: Buffalo leads the NFL at 31.9 points per game and averages 399.7 yards, while Miami ranks 31st at 16.4 points per game. Miami enters after a frustrating 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts, but rookie Kyle McCord provided one of the few encouraging developments in what has been a difficult season to say the least. Making his first NFL start, McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards without an interception and added a three-yard rushing touchdown as the Dolphins rallied from a 21-7 third-quarter deficit. Miami also scored on a 59-yard Chris Johnson interception return and got 76 rushing yards from Ollie Gordon II , but McCord’s fumble near his own goal line was recovered for an Indianapolis touchdown. The kicking game also proved costly as Zane Gonzalez missed two field goals and an extra point in a two-point defeat. Buffalo, meanwhile, continued its surge with a 31-12 road victory over the New York Jets, turning a relatively close 10-6 halftime lead into a convincing win. Josh Allen completed 11 of 21 passes for 196 yards, one touchdown and one interception, but again did major damage with his legs, scoring twice on one-yard runs before hitting DJ Moore for a 45-yard touchdown in the third quarter. James Cook III supplied the knockout punch, finishing with 157 yards on 18 carries and breaking a 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. Buffalo’s defense kept the Jets out of the end zone entirely, and the Bills have allowed just 28 total points over their last three games. The rivalry itself provides Miami with at least some reason for optimism, even though Buffalo has controlled it for much of the Josh Allen era. The Bills have won four of the last five meetings, but the Dolphins snapped a lengthy skid in emphatic fashion the last time these teams played, beating Buffalo 30-13 in Miami on Nov. 9, 2025. away.blurb: Benford suffered a groin injury on Sunday against the New York Jets. He did not return to the game and has not practiced on Wednesday or Thursday. This season, he and rookie Davison Igbinosun lead Bills corners with 33 tackles and Benford is second on the team with eight passes defended. Alford also got banged up against the Jets, suffering a concussion and is currently in the league's protocol, as he made it to the practice field on Thursday, albeit on a limited basis. Earlier in the year, he also missed two games with an ankle injury . The game against the Patriots may be a freebie with quarterback Drake Maye out long-term with an ankle injury, but the other opponents have either dynamic passing attacks or a knack for coming up big in the clutch. That spells trouble for a secondary that has not been tested since the bye. Heading into the Buffalo Bills ' Week 10 game against the Miami Dolphins, the Bills' injury report is full of key contributors , but no other area is struggling with this more than the secondary. Among those injured are cornerbacks Dee Alford and Christian Benford and safety Damar Hamlin. Despite there being a bunch of ailments in the defense's backfield , there may be little concern for Sunday's game against Buffalo's AFC East rival. There are multiple reasons as to why Buffalo should exercise caution with them for Sunday's game, and it is likely in its best interest that the team should do so. What are Benford, Hamlin and Alford dealing with? Hamlin, meanwhile, is dealing with a toe injury, and his run defense is vital to the team's success. However, behind Cole Bishop and trade acquisition Amani Hooker, Hamlin's defensive snap count dropped from 44 in Week 9 to 17 in Week 10 (92% to 24%). While these wounds may be troublesome on paper, when one sees the circumstances, people can breathe easy. Miami passing game lacks legitimacy The Dolphins will start quarterback Kyle McCord in his second career start, which has to be music to the ears of Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard, who has Buffalo's defense on an outstanding pace since the bye week. McCord went 17-of-32 passing for 209 yards in Week 10 against the Indianapolis Colts, and on Sunday, the biggest mismatch will be up front. Miami's offense allows the second-highest pressure rate in the NFL, while the Bills' defense pressures opposing passers at the fifth-highest rate. If Buffalo's front can rattle McCord, the secondary won't be tested against a Miami receiving core that features three rookies, and it'll help the injured defensive backs and youngsters like Igbinosun and 2025 first-rounder Maxwell Hairston prepare for what is to come. away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published Nov 18, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Ala

away.blurb: Kiffin's return to Tennessee Center Aaron Brewer (concussion), punter Bradley Pinion (right groin), cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee), safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) all did not practice. Miami also made a move to sign a punter to the practice squad, bringing in Jack Browning. That is not a guarantee that Pinion will be out, but it is an insurance move for sure. The rest of the DNP players might be upgraded on the additional injury reports. Long snapper Tucker (shoulder), wide receiver Chris Bell (knee), cornerback Juju Brents (neck), wide receiver Caleb Douglas (shoulder), and center Andrew Meyer (neck) were all limited. What makes this list of players concerning is that Meyer was limited. The Dolphins are already down Brewer, and losing Meyer would put the team in a tough spot regarding their center situation. Miami will need to have its top players available if they want a chance to hang with the surging Bills. Defensive lineman Zach Sieler was already out for the season with a ruptured biceps, and he has now been joined by both Zeek Biggers and Jordan Phillips. The full injury report is as follows: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley confirmed on Wednesday that Brewer remains in concussion protocol, so he may very well not be able to play against the Bills. Bell missed Week 10 after banging his surgically repaired knee in practice leading up to the Indianapolis Colts. Douglas was also wearing a red no-contact jersey at practice, indicating that his shoulder may be a bit significant. The same thing can be said of Douglas if he were to miss Week 11. He has been one of the biggest surprises of the 2026 season, as he leads all rookie receivers with 61.2 yards per game on average. Things might already be very tough, considering the Dolphins' defense took a major hit this past week. Biggers suffered a meniscus injury that will now require surgery, ending his season. Phillips also suffered a biceps injury , and he will also be done for the rest of the 2026 season. In just two short weeks, the Dolphins lost three solid defensive linemen. This will lead to Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr. presumably stepping in as starters.

home.headline: Buffalo Bills Handed Concerning Injury News on $72M Starter
home.blurb: ESPN Analyst Calls Out Bills QB Josh Allen: ‘Obviously Playing Worse' Buffalo Bills Handed Concerning Injury News on $72M Starter Unlock the latest Heavy on Bills news — direct to your inbox. The Buffalo Bills could be without an impact starter on Sunday against the New York Jets . Buffalo's offensive line has been hindered by injuries as of late. Starting right tackle Spencer Brown missed the game two weeks ago. Then, last week, starting left tackle Dion Dawkins and starting left guard Alec Anderson were inactive due to injuries. The Bills will now go on the road to play the Jets on Sunday. Buffalo Bills Get Concerning Injury News on Spencer Brown Bills get injury news on Spencer Brown. Buffalo got Brown back from injury last week but he once again could be inactive on Sunday. Brown is in the midst of a four-year, $72 million deal and is a key part of the offensive line. However, he's been on the injury report again, and The Athletic's Joe Buscagalia believes it's unlikely he will be playing on Sunday. "Starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who has been trying to play through a back injury he suffered against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5, was not on the practice field at all. … Brown suffered an ankle injury early in Monday's game and gutted through the rest of the evening. After practice, Brown was in the huddle with his teammates, but he was in sandals with a big wrap on his right ankle," Buscagalia wrote . "It wouldn't be stunning if they are playing the long game to give him rest for the back and ankle injuries, given his importance and the Bills' being on a short week. They also have another short week on the horizon, taking on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 12 on Thanksgiving with only three days after their Week 11 game against the Miami Dolphins. Resting Brown could be important. Missing Thursday's practice is usually not a good sign." If Brown can't go, Tylan Grable will start at right tackle again. Grable replaced Brown two weeks ago and started at left tackle a week ago. Given that Buffalo is a huge favorite, resting Brown makes sense to make sure he's healthy for the stretch run. Although the Bills are massive favorites against the Jets, Buffalo isn't overlooking them. Bills head coach Joe Brady believes the Jets pose a challenge for them on defense. So, they have to be smart with the football. "When you look at it, you can get caught up in the records, but the records, I think, always lie to you in the NFL; that's why you never can focus on them," Brady said . "So it's going to be a huge challenge for us defensively as a football team and a great opportunity for us." The Bills are 8.5-point favorites on the road against the Jets. Cole Shelton Cole

In somewhat of a surprise, starting tight end Dalton Kincaid, who was already nursing an ankle issue, appeared with a second injury to his thumb, and he did not practice as a result. The severity of the hand problem is not known, but Kincaid has played through more serious injuries in the past. Running back Ray Davis was limited in practice by a hamstring. Wide receiver Keon Coleman (ankle) and third-down running back Ty Johnson (knee) also appeared on Wednesday's practice report with new injuries, but both earned full participant status. Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee New Orleans Saints Praised in Chicago Bears Game Preview Joey Hickey · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 19, 2026 at 4:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New Orleans Saints (3-6) take on the Chicago Bears on Sunday. It's not a matchup many Saints supporters are excited about seeing. The Bears are an NFC title contender, while the Saints have repeatedly squandered opportunities to take over the NFC South from the Carolina Panthers (4-5). Still, there are reasons for optimism that go in the Saints' favor. Mike Moraitis of Chicago Bears on Si noted what the Bears will need to watch out for against the Saints this weekend. Per Moraitis, the Saints' wide receiver corps could put the greatest strain on the Bears defense. Here's some of what Moraitis had to say about New Orleans' three top receivers. "The Saints already had a solid one-two punch at wide receiver in Chris Olave and the ascending Devaugh Vele, but New Orleans added rookie Jordyn Tyson into the mix a few weeks ago. Tyson was on the shelf for the first seven games because of a hamstring injury. After a quiet game in his NFL debut, Tyson emerged in Week 10 with 11 catches for 80 yards. Tyson has played the majority of his snaps in the slot, where the Bears have an injury concern this week with Kyler Gordon, who is dealing with a shoulder injury that has him labeled as day-to-day. But, as we noted, Tyson isn't the only one the Bears need to be worried about. Both Vele and Olave are in the midst of career-best seasons and can cause major head aches for a Bears secondary that has seen struggles, and namely with Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson. Luckily for Chicago, rookie Malik Muhammad has been better than expected in his first season and has provided some stability on the outside." While some will write off his impact, we still have only got one game with Travis Etienne Jr. cleared for play at running back since his injury. His effect may take time to be felt, but we could see the beginnings of it this week against the Bears. Add in what the receiver corps is able to do after Tyson's 11-catch breakout game against the Panthers last weekend, and New Orleans could finally start to generate the offense we hoped to see when Tyson was drafted. The Saints haven't been far off from playing playoff caliber football, but the frustration has been mounting as we wait for it to finally happen. New Orleans will get its shot against the Bears.

away.headline: New Orleans Saints injury report: Tyson still limited, Kamara returns
away.blurb: Wednesday’s initial report listed seven non-participants and two limited participants, and today’s report saw only one player upgraded. Veteran running back Alvin Kamara participated in full today after being listed as out for non-injury-related/personal matters yesterday. Otherwise, it’s pretty much the same, with rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson still limited with a chest injury. Along with Tyson, cornerback Decamerio Richardson was limited with a thigh injury. The New Orleans Saints submitted their second injury report of the week on Thursday ahead of their Week 11 contest with the Chicago Bears. Cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) were non-participants on defense, along with multiple offensive line starters: center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), and Asim Richards (knee), who had been filling in for Fuaga. away.headline: Same 10 on Saints Injury Report: Reid & Saints Part
away.blurb: - Emerson will be in concussion protocol and will probably be out for Sunday - Richards is in the same boat as McCoy, except he's a week ahead. We expect him to be limited later this week. - Werner's hammie will keep him out at least this Sunday LIke Wednesday, we expect both to be a full participant by the end of this week and available against the Bears on Sunday. Gordon is considered day-to-day after going down with the injured shoulder against Tampa Bay a week and a half ago. Though the team is not sharing, it is generally considered that he will sit out the Saints game with a short work week for Chicago, who will be playing on Thanksgiving Day against the Lions. Saints vs. Panthers Inactives: Who's Out for Sunday's NFC South Showdown? The New Orleans Saints and Chicago Bears released their second injury report of the week as part of the lead up to Sunday's game between the two at Soldier Field in the Windy City, but one of those on the report superceded any injuries by either team. For the second day in a row, Saints safety Justin Reid was on the report as missing practice on a personal matter, not injury related. This afternoon the story broke that Reid and the team had agreed to go their separate ways. More on Reid's Departure, DC Staley's reaction, and Reid's Replacement Howden's Side of things The numbers didn't change on either team's Thursday practice report. A half-dozen did not participate in practice today for New Orleans Thursday, including the soon-to-be-departed Reid. Cornerback Martin Emerson - concussion Tackle Taliese Fuaga - knee injury Center Eric McCoy - biceps injury Safety Justin Reid - covered above Tackle Asim Richards - bum knee Linebacker Pete Werner - hamstring Much like what we saw Wednesday and Monday, - McCoy's injury will take two-to-three weeks to heal, not enough to put on the IR, but enough to keep him idle the next couple of games Cornerback Decamerion Richardson - thigh Wide receiver Jordyn Tyson - chest Running back CJ Donaldson - shoulder Running back Alvin Kamara - not injury related on Wednesday. It was a day of rest. The Chicago list was identical to Wednesday's, when they didn't hold a complete practice, only a walkthrough. The Bears injury report was half as long as the Saints and not nearly as severe. Cornerback Kyler Gordon - shoulder Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons - knee Simmons practice on Monday, sat our Tuesday, and was part of the walkthroughs Wednesday. home.headline: Chicago Bears breathe sigh of relief after latest Jeffery Simmons injury update
home.blurb: Which is why the franchise was forced to hold their breath on Wednesday. Their defensive superstar was listed as limited on the injury report with a knee problem. While the Bears didn’t technically practice, seeing Simmons listed at all led to concern. Simmons will need to get on the practice field to truly prove he can play through whatever is bothering him. But defensive coordinator Dennis Allen isn’t expecting the defensive tackle to be limited in what he can do whatsoever, via Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune. “Bears DT Jeffery Simmons popped up on the estimated injury report as “limited” with a knee issue yesterday,” Biggs wrote. “DC Dennis Allen said he does not anticipate any issues with Simmons’ availability.” It hasn’t taken long for the Chicago Bears to see how valuable Jeffery Simmons is to their franchise. They aren’t surprised though, seeing as the franchise traded away two firsts and a fourth-round pick for the All-Pro defensive tack. In his first two games, Simmons has already put up 10 tackles, two pass break ups and two sacks. Through his nine games total in 2026, the defensive tackle has registered 48 tackles, 11 quarterback hits, six pass break ups and six sacks. It’s not hard to see why Simmons is so valuable to Chicago’s defense and team overall. The defensive tackle’s status on Chicago’s Week 11 injury reports moving forward will be heavily monitored. But the Bears are already breathing their sigh of relief. Chicago Bears not fearing serious Jeffery Simmons injury The Bears remain focused on winning as many games as possible. But they also have their eyes set on the playoffs. Should Chicago qualify, they want their roster to be maximum capacity health wise. Players like Joe Thuney and Grady Jarrett already receive consistent veteran rest days. As Simmons tries to shake off whatever is bothering him with his knee, the Bears are trying to be as cautious as they can. If the defensive tackle were to miss time, even if just one game, Chicago would be dealt a massive blow. But it doesn’t appear Simmons’ current ailment will keep him off his feet long. home.headline: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears
home.blurb: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Kiffin's return to Tennessee 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears Sheesh. The New Orleans Saints (3-6) shared a lengthy injury report ahead of Sunday's game with the Chicago Bears (7-2), with seven players not participating and two other limited to start the week. They'll need all hands on deck for a chance at upsetting one of the hottest teams in the NFL. Let's hope they can get it done. And let's start with the good news. Rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) returned to full practice reps on Wednesday after missing several games between that shoulder injury and a stint in concussion protocol. We haven't seen him since the rookie exited Week 9's game in Paris against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Donaldson has been a productive rusher for New Orleans on limited snaps (averaging 4.8 yards per carry and a team-high 64.7% success rate), and he was just starting to earn a bigger role after initially getting on the field as a short-yardage specialist. He competes hard in pass protection, too. How snaps could be divided between him, Travis Etienne Jr., Alvin Kamara (more on him in a minute), and Audric Estime remains to be seen. What about those seven players who didn't practice? We expected Kamara (not injury related) would get his usual rest day, which has been a pattern since he suffered a Week 5 back injury. He turned 31 this summer and has worn a lot of tread off his tires so it makes sense to give him a lighter workload during the week, especially if he's going to have a reduced role on game days. Kamara was only on the field last Sunday for 16 snaps but he scored two touchdowns. Veteran safety Justin Reid (not injury related) did not practice on Wednesday due to a personal matter, and head coach Kellen Moore was noncommittal when asked if Reid was expected back on Thursday. Stay tuned. Backup right tackle Asim Richards (knee) and a couple of defensive starters who got nicked up against the Carolina Panthers -- cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) -- were held out of practice. Additionally, starting right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) and center Erik McCoy (biceps) both did not practice, though Moore said "we'll see" if either of them can return to work later this week. Two other players were limited to start the week: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest), who you can read more about here ; and backup corner Decamerion Richardson (thigh). We'll be watching for updates on their status as the week continues. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 11 picks, including the Jaguars to handle the Giants on the road Imagn Images Stacking winning weeks is always a good feeling when it comes to picking NFL games . I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. Pick: Texans 30, Colts 27 Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. As Saleh himself said after the team's latest loss, you aren't going to win allowing 40 points a game. The Titans' previous two opponents have crossed the 40 mark, and Dallas, in spite of their loss, score as much against a better 49ers defense this past week. Dallas is a veteran-led group in the middle of a difficult year; their down season can't be compared to that of the Titans, and QB Dak Prescott is sure to run this defense through the ringer. On the road after arguably their worst showing of the year, Saleh's defense has their back against the wall. Prediction: Titans win, 30-27 With that said, I still think the Titans find a way to pull this one out. If the away team can strike a balance between their growing offensive attack and a defense that isn't allowing Dallas to do whatever they want, a close win is in the cards. The Titans have yet to play a full, complete game this year. Even their Week 6 victory over the Indianapolis Colts saw Tennessee trailing 13-0 at halftime. I'm predicting that the Titans get this done, and do so by offering a solid showing through all four quarters. That means a consistent Cam Ward, a defense that bends, but doesn't break, reliable play-calling on either side of the ball, and at least a little good luck on the injury front. A lot has to go right, but this game wouldn't have been seen as winnable only a few short weeks ago. For that reason, I believe the Titans will win it. Tennessee enters the Week 11 matchup at 1-8, while Dallas sits at 4-6 and is desperate to get back on track after another defensive collapse. Despite their records, both teams have reasons to believe they can make this an interesting matchup. The Titans have shown signs of offensive improvement in recent weeks, particularly behind running back Tony Pollard. Meanwhile, Dallas has one of the league's most productive offenses but continues to struggle defensively. Here's a look at the matchup and what several national analysts are predicting: Score (if applicable) Matt Bowen (ESPN) Mike Clay (ESPN) Seth Wickersham (ESPN) Bill Bender (Sporting News) Vinnie Iyer (Sporting News) Pete Prisco (CBS Sports) Albert Breer (Sports Illustrated) Nate Davis (USA Today) Nick Brinkerhoff (USA Today) The Titans are coming off a 40-23 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, their third consecutive defeat. However, the offense has shown some improvement. Tennessee has topped 300 total yards in three straight games and is averaging 5.8 yards per play over its last three contests. Pollard has been a major part of that progress. He has rushed for 628 yards and six touchdowns on 142 carries this season, averaging 4.4 yards per attempt. Over his last three games, Pollard has totaled 279 rushing yards, 112 receiving yards and six touchdowns. Second-year quarterback Cam Ward has also shown signs of growth. Through nine games, he has completed 63.8% of his passes for 1,714 yards, eight touchdowns and six interceptions. He'll face a Dallas defense that has struggled mightily against opposing offenses. With that said, the Cowboys likely have too much offensive firepower for Tennessee to consistently keep pace. Pollard should find opportunities against a Dallas defense that has been particularly vulnerable against the run, but Prescott and the Cowboys' passing attack should ultimately make the difference. The Titans have enough offensive momentum to make things interesting, especially if they can control the clock, but Dallas is expected to come away with the victory. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Tennessee Titans (1-8) travel to AT&T Stadium on Sunday afternoon for a matchup with the Dallas Cowboys (4-6). This is a must win for Dallas should they hope to stay within reach of the first-place Giants in the NFC East while Tennessee is looking to see continued growth from their young quarterback, Cam Ward . Each team takes the field looking to snap a losing streak. The Titans have dropped three straight and sit last in the AFC South, while Dallas is in second place in the NFC East and as noted, needs a win this weekend to remain in the postseason conversation. Tennessee has had issues scoring touchdowns (18.6 points/game), but this is not expected to be a low-scoring affair. Dallas ranks sixth in scoring at 28.6 points per game, but the Cowboys are allowing 28.2 points and a league-worst 406.3 yards per game. The Titans’ defense is nearly as generous, allowing 405.6 yards per game. Tennessee’s latest loss was a 40-23 defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars, dropping the Titans to 1-8 despite periods of competitive football. The Titans trailed only 16-10 at halftime and stayed within 23-16 entering the fourth quarter before Jacksonville finally pulled away. Tennessee totaled 342 yards but converted only 18 percent of its third downs, while its defense surrendered 459 yards, 26 first downs and 40 points. Cam Ward threw touchdown passes to Daniel Bellinger and Tony Pollard , with the latter going for 32 yards to pull Tennessee within 30-23 midway through the fourth, while Joey Slye connected on field goals of 54, 53 and 50 yards. But Trevor Lawrence carved up the Titans for 352 yards and three touchdowns, and Jacksonville scored the final 10 points to put the game away. Dallas is coming off an even wilder game, a 46-40 home loss to the San Francisco 49ers. The game was not as close as the final score. The 49ers accumulated 584 total yards, the most Dallas has ever allowed in a home game, averaged 9.4 yards per play and produced three touchdowns of at least 66 yards. Christian McCaffrey alone amassed 223 scrimmage yards and three scores as Dallas’ late comeback fell short. Dak Prescott completed 58.8 percent of his throws for 343 yards and five touchdowns, matching his career high for touchdown passes, and George Pickens erupted for 11 catches, 145 yards and three scores. CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy each caught touchdowns as Dallas piled up 439 yards, but the Cowboys simply couldn’t stop San Francisco. The central storyline Sunday is whether Tennessee can take advantage of a Dallas defense that has been dominated nearly every week this season. The Cowboys are allowing a league-worst 154.1 rushing yards per game, potentially creating an avenue for Tennessee to protect Ward, lean on its backfield and keep Prescott off the field. These teams have alternated wins in each of their last five meetings: Dallas won 27-13 in 2022, Tennessee won 28-14 at AT&T Stadium in 2018, the Cowboys won 26-10 in 2014, the Titans won 34-27 in 2010 and Dallas won 45-14 in 2006. away.headline: Titans announce unfortunate injury news for rookie WR Carnell Tate
away.blurb: Tennessee Titans rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate missed the first game of his NFL career in Week 8, ruled out with a shoulder injury. The Titans officially ruled Tate out for Sunday’s Week 10 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. With Tate out again this weekend, Cam Ward and the Tennessee offense will continue to lean on Wan’Dale Robinson, Chimere Dike, Elic Ayomanor and Calvin Ridley as their WR options. Tate, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, had an extra week to recover over the Titans’ bye. However, he was unable to take the practice field for any action this week as he continues to deal with the lingering issue. “I was really optimistic going through the bye week. It’s just, the shoulder’s stuck on him a little bit,” head coach Robert Saleh said when speaking to reporters on Friday. “We’re hopeful for next week, but I’ll have a better answer for you guys come Wednesday.” After a relatively slow start to his NFL career, Tate exploded for 145 yards on nine catches in a Week 4 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. The former Ohio State standout logged his first professional touchdown in a win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6. Through seven games in his first season with the Titans, Tate has 34 catches for 413 yards and one score. Sunday’s game against the Jaguars will kick off at 1 p.m. ET. Mayfield has had a rough start to the 2026 campaign with more interceptions (four) than passing touchdowns (three). However, he's still a better option under center than undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who took first-team reps in practice Wednesday for the Buccaneers. Daniels, who has already started three games this season due to injury issues for Mayfield, has also thrown for more interceptions (five) than touchdowns (three). Tampa Bay subsequently has not been very proficient through the air this season. In fact, Todd Bowles’ squad ranks league worst in several passing categories: attempts (240), yards (1,277) and touchdowns (six). Meanwhile, on defense, Winfield is one of the Buccaneers’ very best players. A two-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro, the longtime Tampa Bay defender has been especially stout against the run in 2026. The 2020 second-round pick has earned an 85.5 Pro Football Focus grade for his efforts against the run, the 13th-best run-defense mark among 100 qualified safeties. Additionally, he hasn't been too shabby against the pass, and has allowed just five receptions all season. And for his efforts in coverage, he's earned a 67.7 grade from PFF, the 24th-best pass-coverage mark among all qualified safeties. Consequently, the Buccaneers, which stand at just 3-6, would hardly be in an optimal situation playing without both Winfield and Mayfield on Sunday. As for the Lions, they will be down two of their defensive captains and very best players in Week 11: LB Jack Campbell (neck) and EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (ACL). Hutchinson has already been ruled out for the rest of the season, while Campbell is highly unlikely to suit up again in 2026. Detroit, however, is getting back its All-Pro safety for its tilt with Tampa Bay: Kerby Joseph. Joseph – who was activated off the physically unable to perform list Wednesday – hasn't played a single snap since Week 6 of the 2025 season due to a lingering knee issue. Per Lions head man Dan Campbell, Joseph will be on a “pitch count” Sunday, but is still expected to log more snaps than fellow safety Brian Branch did when he returned from his Achilles’ tear earlier this season. Branch played 45 total defensive snaps in his season debut in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers. Prior to Joseph's chronic knee ailment , he was a ball-hawk safety. In 55 career games, he's secured 20 interceptions, including a league-high nine during his All-Pro campaign in 2024. If he can come even remotely close to replicating that level of production, he'll provide a big boost to the back-end of the Lions’ defense. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 76 percent chance to capture the Week 11 victory. But this time it will be different! Remember, a broken clock is right twice a day. Anyway, Detroit will have a few challenges in this one, including facing a tough Tampa Bay defense a week after having to play a game in Germany. The Lions’ explosive offense had trouble generating points against Green Bay, Minnesota, and Miami (the Dolphins!) before bouncing back against the Patriots last week. Perhaps Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles could use some of those blueprints to slow down star running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Also, this will be the Lions’ first game without star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who sustained a season-ending knee injury against the Patriots. Peter Dewey Week 11 Upset Pick Baltimore Ravens (+114) vs. Carolina Panthers If you’re going to make a case for an upset this week where there are five teams favored by double digits, I don’t mind targeting the Baltimore Ravens in their clash with the Carolina Panthers. Carolina barely came away with a win over a bad New Orleans team in Week 10, and it remains pretty banged up on both sides of the ball. The Panthers are a top-10 team in the league in EPA/Play on offense, but they’re in the middle of the pack in EPA/Play on the defensive side of the ball. Carolina is also allowing 4.4 yards per carry on the ground, so this could be the week Derrick Henry gets going. The Ravens are coming off a pretty huge loss at home against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night, but Jacoby Brissett wasn’t bad in that matchup, and he may have led this Baltimore team to a win had Zay Flowers not lost a costly fumble late in the fourth quarter. Reed, Kerby Joseph, Devin White, and Jack Campbell, who are on the injured list. It's enough to convince me that now is the time to sell your Lions' stock. Detroit now has to take on a Buccaneers team that's fresh off a BYE week, and that ranks in the top five in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. While the Lions' offense is certainly elite, they're going to struggle to rack up the amount of points they need to aid their limping defense. Baker Mayfield's injury status is up in the air, which could make this bet tough to win, but if he plays, we're in a great spot. Even if he doesn't, Tampa Bay can win this game with their defense and rushing attack alone. They're my upset pick of the week. Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee Three Bold Predictions for Lions vs. Buccaneers in Week Eleven (REUTERS) Dakota Allen · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 19, 2026 at 10:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Returning from a 35-10 rout of the New England Patriots in Munich, the 7-2 Detroit Lions welcome the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers to Ford Field this Sunday at 1:00 PM ET. While Detroit sits atop a fiercely contested NFC North on a five-game winning streak, Tampa Bay arrives off its Week ten bye as one of the NFL's strangest statistical anomalies. The Buccaneers boast the league's No. 1 rushing offense (163.9 yards per game) and No. 1 run defense (79.1 yards allowed per game) yet rank dead last in passing offense (141.9 yards per game) while dealing with a foot strain that puts quarterback Baker Mayfield's availability in question. With strength meeting strength in the trenches and Detroit looking to stay undefeated at Ford Field, here are three bold predictions for Sunday's NFC clash. 1. Jahmyr Gibbs Eclipses 150 Scrimmage Yards Against the NFL's Top Run Defense On paper, running the ball against Todd Bowles' front seven looks like a losing proposition. Tampa Bay surrenders just 3.5 yards per carry and has allowed a league-low three rushing touchdowns all season. However, Detroit offensive coordinator Drew Petzing will not abandon the ground game, instead, he will weaponize Jahmyr Gibbs in space. Fresh off an NFC-leading 252-scrimmage-yard explosion in Germany, Gibbs will find daylight via perimeter zone runs, screens, and wheel routes out of the backfield. Even if Tampa Bay's interior line clogs up early down dives, expect Gibbs to crack 150 total yards and score at least once, becoming the first player all year to single-handedly unravel the Buccaneers' run-stopping formula. 2. Detroit's Defense Holds Tampa Bay Under 100 Rushing Yards and Forces Three Turnovers Tampa Bay's offensive identity hinges entirely on Bucky Irving and a ground attack averaging 5.0 yards per attempt. That formula works when games stay close, but it collapses when trailing inside a deafening Ford Field. Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit, currently ranking fourth in the NFL against the run at 90.4 yards allowed per game, will sell out to load the box on early downs. Whether a hobbled Baker Mayfield guts it out or undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels steps under center, the Buccaneers' 32nd-ranked passing attack will be forced into obvious third-and-long passing situations. Once Detroit's pass rush pins its ears back, look for Alim McNeill and company to force three takeaways and snap Tampa Bay's streak of dominant ground performances. 3. Jameson Williams Outscores Amon-Ra St. Brown as Detroit Wins by Three Scores Because Tampa Bay routinely commits extra defenders toward the line of scrimmage to suffocate intermediate zones, single-high safety looks will be there for the taking downfield. While Amon-Ra St. Brown will draw heavy bracket coverage and Antoine Winfield Jr.'s constant attention between the hashes, Jared Goff, coming off a 303-yard, three-touchdown clinic, will repeatedly test the Buccaneers' boundary corners over the top. Jameson Williams has quietly been building momentum, and Sunday sets up as his signature vertical breakout of the 2026 campaign. Predict Williams to haul in two touchdowns of 40-plus yards, outpacing St. Brown in fantasy and box-score production as the Lions cruise to a comfortable victory. away.headline: Buccaneers at Lions: Initial injury report for Week 11
away.blurb: Mayfield (foot/right thumb) was held out of Wednesday’s session after suffering an injury to his foot and ankle area during the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Chicago Bears. Aside from Mayfield, safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) was the only other Buccaneer held out of practice Wednesday. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee), who missed Tampa Bay’s game against Chicago, was a limited participant. Cornerback Josh Hayes (knee), tight end Cade Otton (thumb) and left tackle Tristan Wirfs (toe) participated fully. Cornerbacks D.J. Reed (hip) and Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder) were among six players listed as limited, while safety Kerby Joseph (knee) was listed as a full participant. home.headline: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury
home.blurb: "Nothing new," Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game when asked for an update on Hutchinson. "We’ll know more when we get back to the States. But any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out." This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury Initial tests on Aidan Hutchinson’s injured knee showed the Detroit Lions star has a torn ACL, according to a report from NFL Network on Monday, Nov. 16. Hutchinson, 26, had initial tests performed in Germany, where the Lions beat the New England Patriots on Sunday, and will have more done in the United States, the report added. On Good Morning Football, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said, “my understanding, the belief is it’s a torn ACL and more for Aidan Hutchinson.” The injury to Hutchinson occurred in the first quarter of Detroit’s win over the Patriots. Hutchinson sacked quarterback Drake Maye and leapt into the air to celebrate. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right knee. Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side. Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday. If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

He's allowed one sack and 11 pressures in those chances. For someone who started off at left guard, then switched back to center and watched Mays momentarily take back over, it's impressive. Top cornerback D.J. Reed (hip) was also going through drills. And while everything remains up in the air for his availability, it doesn't sound like Reed will play against the Buccaneers. Add in the Thanksgiving short week coming off of Sunday's game against Tampa Bay, and it makes all the more sense to stay patient. Dorsey and Rakestraw have continued to have a role in the secondary with Reed on the sideline. Seeing both of those players log back-to-back practices to start the week is a good sign. Returning safety Kerby Joseph was a full participant to start the week. He's back on the 53-man roster after getting activated, and the Lions are thrilled to finally get him back playing . The Cards are floundering, battling an inordinate number of injuries at the skill positions, and now starting rookie Carson Beck at quarterback. Meanwhile, Patrick Mahomes has the Chiefs in first in the AFC West and just one game behind Buffalo for the top spot in the AFC (Spoiler Alert: the Bills and Chiefs play on Thanksgiving on NBC/Peacock .) It should come as no surprise that the statistical gap is significant: the Cardinals average just 18.4 points per game while allowing 28.9, whereas Kansas City scores 26.3 per game and owns one of the league’s stingiest defenses at 17.3 points allowed per game…and KC is undefeated at home this season (4-0). The Cardinals are coming off an ugly 34-6 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams, a game in which their offense essentially disappeared after the opening quarter. Two 49-yard field goals from Chad Ryland gave Arizona a 6-3 lead, but those would be its only points. Beck, making his first NFL start, completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards with two interceptions, while the Cardinals managed only 142 total yards, 34 rushing yards and six first downs. They went 0-for-6 on third down and held the ball for just 17:37. Trey McBride led the team with five catches for 37 yards. The Chiefs delivered a performance that was basically the exact opposite of that put forth by the Cards. KC rolled past the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 for their second straight win. Mahomes was sensational, completing 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns without throwing an interception. Rookie Emmett Johnson carried the ball 22 times for 101 yards and also caught a touchdown pass, helping Kansas City pile up 461 yards of total offense. The Kansas City defense forced two turnovers and held Atlanta to one touchdown in five red-zone trips. These teams do not meet often, but the recent regular-season history decidedly favors Kansas City. The Chiefs have won the last two meetings, including a 44-21 victory at Arizona in the 2022 season opener, when Mahomes threw five touchdown passes, and a 26-14 win at Arrowhead Stadium in 2018; the Cardinals’ last regular-season victory in the series was 17-14 in 2014.
