picks.headline: Chiefs-Cardinals betting line & prediction: Kansas City’s biggest mismatch yet?
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. Kansas City enters 7-2, while Arizona has lost two straight to fall to 3-7. The betting line lists the Chiefs as 15.5-point favorites over the Cardinals. The prediction picks Kansas City to beat Arizona 33-9 and cover the spread. The Kansas City Chiefs won their second game in a row Sunday when they overpowered the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 , improving to 7-2 on the NFL season. The Arizona Cardinals lost their second straight 34-6 to the Los Angeles Rams to drop to 3-7. Here’s what to know about their matchup on Sunday ... How to watch Cardinals at Chiefs Kickoff: Noon Central Where: Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -15.5 Behind the ARI-KC matchup While the Chiefs were getting back on track by taking care of business against the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons over the past two weeks, the Cardinals have been falling apart at the seams. Sunday’s monumental mismatch starts at the quarterback position, where rookie Carson Beck is expected to make his second career start after completing just 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards and two interceptions against the Rams. Arizona has turned to Beck after trading Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens and watching last year’s Chiefs backup Gardner Minshew tear the UCL in his throwing arm. Understanding the reality of the situation, linebacker Drue Tranquill showed the two-time national champion with Georgia some respect before outlining the problems he may face against a Chiefs defense that has come alive with eight sacks over the last two games. “He’s obviously got winning pedigree — he did it in college,” Tranquill said of Beck. “He’ll get another start under his belt this week in a great environment, so it’s a good opportunity for him, but we’ll have to execute our pre-snap looks, have to execute our game plan in terms of owning our leverage, taking away options he might want to go to early in the down. And then hopefully, as the game progresses, we can get the pass rush going, get them in known passing situations and get them on the ground.” With running back Jeremiyah Love, the No. 3 overall pick, on injured reserve, the Cardinals’ best path to an upset is extending possessions with veteran back Tyler Allgeier and utilizing first-team All-Pro tight end Trey McBride. McBride has managed 78 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns despite Arizona’s struggles. With wide receivers Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Michael Wilson (neck) out for the remainder of the season, that’s left McBride as Beck’s lone viable option. Among Arizona’s available players, tight end Elijah Higgins ranks second on the team in receiving yards with 18 catches for 162 yards. “They’ve got some good tight ends, and so we’ll have to be on it,” Tranquill said. “They’re big, they’re physical, can make contested catches. And so we’ll have to own our leverage and be physical at the top of the stem and not allow them to create separation, and try to get the ball off these guys.” Arizona’s protection has allowed 28 sacks this season — tied for the sixth-most in the league. Meanwhile, Chiefs defensive lineman George Karlaftis enters Sunday with at least one sack in each of his last three games , Ashton Gillotte is in the midst of a two-game sack streak and Chris Jones has registered 2.5 sacks over the last two games. The Cardinals’ offensive line is a point to watch, as they played against the Rams without starting center Hjalte Froholdt (concussion) and left tackle Jayden Williams (knee), who had already replaced left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. (biceps tear). Both Froholdt and Williams were limited in practice Wednesday. The situation doesn’t get any easier for the Cardinals on the other side of the ball. In the run game, the Cardinals allow 4.2 yards per carry, and through the air, they give up 8.2 yards per pass attempt. The Chiefs opted to rest Kenneth Walker last Sunday against the Falcons because of groin tightness, and he didn’t practice Wednesday . That means rookie Emmett Johnson could make his second straight start after compiling 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in Atlanta. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes is coming off his best passing stat line of the season, in which he threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns against the Falcons. But bigger than that were the chunk gains, as the outing included seven completions of 20 yards or more. While the Cardinals’ secondary is susceptible to explosive passing plays, if there is one area of concern for the Chiefs, it’s that they’re more than capable of generating pressure. Led by safety Budda Baker with 3.5 sacks and outside linebackers Zaven Collins and Josh Sweat with three apiece, the Cardinals have registered 21 sacks this season. “They do a great job of causing havoc and causing pressure, and they do a great job throughout a lot of these football games of kind of stopping the offenses,” Mahomes said. “There’s been parts where offenses have kind of found the big plays, and it has to come within rhythm. It’s not like you can kind of hunt those things. You have to get the ball out of your hand, because if you don’t, they’ll get home, and they’ll cause negative plays.” Protection will be imperative for what could be a shorthanded Chiefs offensive line. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion) both missed practice Wednesday, and it remains to be seen whether newly signed veteran Fred Johnson can provide a boost after joining Kansas City’s practice squad Tuesday. In his opening game in a Kansas City uniform , wide receiver Josh Downs turned 11 snaps into four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown. Wide receiver Rashee Rice led the Chiefs with 82 yards, and Downs, Andrew Armstrong and rookie Cyrus Allen all reached the end zone. Sunday’s game will give way to a short Thanksgiving week for the Chiefs, with perhaps their most important game of the season awaiting them Thursday night against the Buffalo Bills. Given the grand disparity between the two clubs, look for head coach Andy Reid to be mindful about how long he plays some of his key contributors, especially those dealing with injuries. Cardinals-Chiefs game prediction In my 13 years analyzing and previewing Chiefs games, I’m not sure that I can recall a matchup this lopsided going in. But as they say, that’s why they play the games. away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals have their starting quarterback battling through an injury heading into the Week 11 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. Carson Beck popped up on Thursday’s injury report as a limited participant with a back injury. However, he seemed to be walking normally in the locker room after practice that was open to the media. This is not the first time this season that Beck is dealing with a back injury, having dealt with it earlier in the year. The Arizona Cardinals have handed the reigns of the franchise to rookie quarterback Carson Beck. After trading away starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens ahead of the trade deadline, the former Georgia Bulldog has been the franchise’s next hope. While he is looking to improve as he gets more experience, he is dealing with an injury that made him pop up on the injury report. Let’s take a closer look at to what Carson Beck’s injury is and what it means for the Arizona Cardinals. Arizona Cardinals place Carson Beck on Thursday’s injury report Carson Beck struggled last week in his NFL debut against the Los Angeles Rams. He completed 11 of 18 (61.1%) of his passes for 108 yards with zero touchdowns and two interceptions while also being sacked five times. The Arizona Cardinals are dealing with a lot of injuries on the offensive side of the ball, so protecting Carson Beck and moving the football could be a challenge. If Beck is unable to go for Week 11, Josh Johnson and Joey Aguilar are the backups on the roster. However, neither quarterback has been with the Arizona Cardinals for more than two weeks. It will be intriguing to see if Beck is able to improve and if the team can compete against one of the top contenders in the league. ・ Michigan Wolverines Key Player Charged with Indecent Exposure Before Week 12 ・ New Orleans Saints Expected to Release 2x Super Bowl Champion ・ Denver Broncos to Sign Star to Major 4-Year Extension ・ Texas A&M Aggies: Marcel Reed Named Most Disappointing QB of 2026 Season The post Arizona Cardinals Add Carson Beck to Injury Report Ahead of Week 11 vs. Kansas City Chiefs appeared first on Gridiron Heroics .

(Injury Update, Betting Impact for Chiefs vs. Falcons in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes took a scary hit in Week 9 against the New York Jets, injuring his elbow in the process. However, Mahomes didn't miss a play in the Chiefs' Week 9 win, and he's off the injury report and expected to start in a road matchup with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. Patrick Mahomes (knee, right elbow) not listed on injury report for Week 10. Oddsmakers have expected Mahomes to play in this game from the jump, as the Chiefs opened as three-point favorites on the road in Week 10. They remain favored by three at DraftKings Sportsbook as they look to get to 7-2 in the 2026 season. picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Las Vegas GP 2026 – Practice 2 TRENDING TNF preview: Texans have hope? Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) head to Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday for a game against their instate rival, the Philadelphia Eagles (2-7). Although on the road, this game comes at a critical point in the Steelers’ season. With games the next three weeks against the Broncos, the Texans, and the Jaguars - all teams contending for a playoff spot in the AFC - this one is a near must-win against the Birds. Second in the AFC North and sixth in the AFC overall, Aaron Rodgers and co. are a half-game ahead of the Browns and 1.5 games ahead of the Patriots in the postseason chase. The Eagles have struggled for most of the season. Jalen Hurts led Philly to wins in their first two games, but the Eagles have since lost every game as well as their quarterback (blood clots). This season, the Steelers have leaned on Rodgers, a productive running game and a defense that ranks among the league leaders in sacks and turnover differential. The veteran signal-caller has thrown for 2,014 yards with 15 touchdowns and six interceptions, while Jaylen Warren has rushed for 719 yards. Philadelphia’s season has unraveled in large part because of injuries, most notably the aforementioned loss of Hurts to injured reserve with blood clots. That leaves Joe Milton III directing an Eagles offense averaging just 16.4 points and an NFL-low 260.2 yards per game. Pittsburgh’s four-game winning streak came to an abrupt end last Sunday in a 38-18 road loss to Cincinnati. The Bengals completely suffocated the Steelers with Pittsburgh managing only 23 total yards through the first three quarters before producing some offense and points after the game was out of reach. DK Metcalf was held without a catch through three quarters before finishing with two receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown, while the defense spent far too much time on the field. Philadelphia, meanwhile, comes into Sunday’s game rested after its bye but desperately searching for an answer to a disastrous stretch. The Eagles’ most recent game was a 19-11 home loss to the Giants on Nov. 8. Milton made his first Eagles start and completed 18 of 34 passes for just 169 yards. It has been a weekly headline for Philadelphia: “Eagles’ are Offensive on Offense”. The bye, though, may help an injury-ravaged roster: receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could return after missing the Giants game. away.headline: Star Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker goes down with thumb injury
away.blurb: Kiffin's return to Tennessee Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen suffered a broken left thumb during the team's game against the Cincinnati Bengals, and Queen intends to play through the injury. He popped up on the injury report with a hand injury Wednesday and was limited at practice. The news was first reported by Chris Halicke of DK Pittsburgh Sports. Queen did not come out of the game once he suffered the injury, and has toughed it out instead. For most of his tenure with the Steelers, Queen has been someone who is willing to play through injuries. The Steelers are dealing with a new injuries coming out of that Bengals game that include Queen, but also outside linebacker Nick Herbig. Herbig was back at practice on Thursday after missing Wednesday's session with hip and rib injuries. While still limited on Thursday, Herbig could be on track to play against the Eagles, even if it is in a limited fashion. Pittsburgh lost starting left guard Mason McCormick to an ankle injury that will knock him out for at least the rest of the regular season. Spencer Anderson is expected to take over his spot. To start the season, Anderson started the first two games at left guard. away.headline: Eagles' LB Zack Baun misses second practice ahead of Steelers game
away.blurb: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Zack Baun missed his second straight practice Thursday with a back injury, while wide receiver DeVonta Smith was upgraded to full participation as the team prepared to host the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. Linebacker Smael Mondon Jr. also sat out Thursday with an ankle injury after being listed as a full participant Wednesday. Jihaad Campbell was listed as a full participant for a second straight day with hamstring and quadriceps injuries. Campbell missed the past two games, and his progress gives the Eagles an option alongside Jeremiah Trotter Jr. if Baun or Mondon is unavailable. Trotter started next to Baun while Campbell was out. The Eagles will issue their game designations Friday. Smith was listed as limited Wednesday in his first practice after the bye. He has missed five of the past six games with a hamstring injury. Dontayvion Wicks remained limited Thursday with an ankle injury that sidelined him for three straight games. Coach Nick Sirianni said Wednesday he was optimistic both receivers could return against Pittsburgh. DeVonta Smith upgraded to full participation Smith’s upgrade is good news for Joe Milton, who will make his second start for Philadelphia. Milton threw for 169 yards and ran for 64 in a 19-11 loss to the New York Giants without Smith or Wicks. Rookie Makai Lemon led the Eagles with six catches for 61 yards in that game. Smith has 26 catches for 310 yards and two touchdowns in four games this season. Elliott was listed on the injury report this week with an ankle injury, though he was a full participant on both November 12 and 13 after initially being limited on November 11, and thus was not listed with a game designation. The Pittsburgh Steelers have lost a key piece of their secondary for a monumental Week 10 showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football. Having to face an explosive Bengals passing offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow as well as the star wide receiver duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins now becomes much tougher of a task for Pittsburgh without Elliott on the field. The Steelers, though, were able to at least hold Cincinnati in check to an extent during their first meeting this season, which resulted in a 30-27 victory for the black and gold at Acrisure Stadium in Week 3. Elliott was not active for that contest either, while residing on the reserve/injured list to open the year after going down with a season-ending knee/hamstring injury in Week 8 of the 2025 campaign. Holding up in coverage as a group on the back end of the defense against the likes of Chase and Higgins would've been a big ask even with Elliott on the field, though, and being down a veteran like that could have reverberating effects when facing a passing offense that averages the most yards per game (285.5) in the league. home.blurb: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Zack Baun missed his second straight practice Thursday with a back injury, while wide receiver DeVonta Smith was upgraded to full participation as the team prepared to host the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. Linebacker Smael Mondon Jr. also sat out Thursday with an ankle injury after being listed as a full participant Wednesday. Jihaad Campbell was listed as a full participant for a second straight day with hamstring and quadriceps injuries. Campbell missed the past two games, and his progress gives the Eagles an option alongside Jeremiah Trotter Jr. if Baun or Mondon is unavailable. Trotter started next to Baun while Campbell was out. The Eagles will issue their game designations Friday. Smith was listed as limited Wednesday in his first practice after the bye. He has missed five of the past six games with a hamstring injury. Dontayvion Wicks remained limited Thursday with an ankle injury that sidelined him for three straight games. Coach Nick Sirianni said Wednesday he was optimistic both receivers could return against Pittsburgh. DeVonta Smith upgraded to full participation Smith’s upgrade is good news for Joe Milton, who will make his second start for Philadelphia. Milton threw for 169 yards and ran for 64 in a 19-11 loss to the New York Giants without Smith or Wicks. Rookie Makai Lemon led the Eagles with six catches for 61 yards in that game. Smith has 26 catches for 310 yards and two touchdowns in four games this season. away.headline: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike misses second practice before Panthers game
away.blurb: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike missed practice for a second straight day Thursday with a hamstring injury, while rookie right guard Vega Ioane was upgraded to full participation ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers . Madubuike left Monday night’s 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers and was ruled out in the third quarter. Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday the Ravens would evaluate how the hamstring responds later in the week. Ioane was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated report with knee and shoulder injuries after leaving the Chargers game in the third quarter. His upgrade is an encouraging sign for an offensive line that helped produce just 16 rushing yards Monday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remained limited with a knee injury. Running back Adam Randall (neck and hamstring), tight end Matt Hibner (hand) and outside linebacker Mike Green (biceps) were listed as full participants for a second straight day. Carolina tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble were listed as limited Thursday with knee injuries after both were listed as nonparticipants Wednesday. Running back Chuba Hubbard returned to full participation after a rest day, and outside linebacker Trevis Gipson (ankle) was upgraded from limited to full. Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and safety Isaiah Simmons (knee) remained out of practice. Young (foot) and cornerbacks Will Lee III (hamstring) and Mike Jackson (groin) were listed as full participants for the second straight day. Jackson remains in his return-to-practice window and would need to be activated from injured reserve to play Sunday. The teams’ Friday reports will provide the official game designations. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey was added to Thursday’s report as a nonparticipant for personal reasons. Minter sent Humphrey home Thursday and said the cornerback will be inactive Sunday. The decision came a day after Humphrey apologized for saying on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” Vega Ioane upgraded to full participation Madubuike’s status is the main injury question for Baltimore heading into Friday. His availability will help determine how the Ravens rotate their interior linemen against Carolina and how much pressure they can generate up the middle against Bryce Young. Humphrey’s absence also changes the coverage rotation against a Panthers receiving group led by Tetairoa McMillan. home.headline: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike misses second practice before Panthers game
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike missed practice for a second straight day Thursday with a hamstring injury, while rookie right guard Vega Ioane was upgraded to full participation ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers . Madubuike left Monday night’s 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers and was ruled out in the third quarter. Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday the Ravens would evaluate how the hamstring responds later in the week. Ioane was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated report with knee and shoulder injuries after leaving the Chargers game in the third quarter. His upgrade is an encouraging sign for an offensive line that helped produce just 16 rushing yards Monday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remained limited with a knee injury. Running back Adam Randall (neck and hamstring), tight end Matt Hibner (hand) and outside linebacker Mike Green (biceps) were listed as full participants for a second straight day. Carolina tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble were listed as limited Thursday with knee injuries after both were listed as nonparticipants Wednesday. Running back Chuba Hubbard returned to full participation after a rest day, and outside linebacker Trevis Gipson (ankle) was upgraded from limited to full. Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and safety Isaiah Simmons (knee) remained out of practice. Young (foot) and cornerbacks Will Lee III (hamstring) and Mike Jackson (groin) were listed as full participants for the second straight day. Jackson remains in his return-to-practice window and would need to be activated from injured reserve to play Sunday. The teams’ Friday reports will provide the official game designations. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey was added to Thursday’s report as a nonparticipant for personal reasons. Minter sent Humphrey home Thursday and said the cornerback will be inactive Sunday. The decision came a day after Humphrey apologized for saying on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” Vega Ioane upgraded to full participation Madubuike’s status is the main injury question for Baltimore heading into Friday. His availability will help determine how the Ravens rotate their interior linemen against Carolina and how much pressure they can generate up the middle against Bryce Young. Humphrey’s absence also changes the coverage rotation against a Panthers receiving group led by Tetairoa McMillan. NFL Confirms Zakee Wheatley Fine for Hit on Jaylen Waddle The NFL's ruling removes any uncertainty about whether Wheatley's contact with Waddle violated league rules. According to the official game play-by-play , Broncos quarterback Bo Nix targeted Waddle on a deep pass from Denver's 24-yard line with 19 seconds left in the opening quarter. Wheatley delivered a hit as Waddle attempted to make the reception, knocking the ball free. Waddle initially got up but subsequently left the field for a concussion evaluation. The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. They kept it competitive for a little more than a half. At halftime the Jets trailed 10 – 6. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 – 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. away.blurb: The New York Jets lost quarterback Geno Smith to an injury in their Week 10 game against the Buffalo Bills, and rookie Cade Klubnik came in to the offense in a division showdown. Smith took a hit late in the first half and did not return for the start of the second half. For a Jets team that needed a clean afternoon against Buffalo, this likely won't help. Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Just win, baby! (By starting fast offensively) The best way to put pressure on a rookie quarterback is to make the Las Vegas offense one-dimensional. Bo Nix and the Broncos offense can do their part by starting Sunday's game fast offensively and finishing drives with touchdowns. We saw glimpses of this against the Carolina Panthers, with some deep shots early by Nix, but Denver had to kick a field goal on the opening drive. Replicate that this Sunday, but finish the opening drive with a touchdown. And then do it again. And then again. Add to the pressure that the Broncos defense will undoubtedly bring on the rookie QB. — Ian St. Clair Get after Fernando Mendoza Last week, Fernando Mendoza got his first career NFL start against a fierce Seattle Seahawks defense. Prior to Mendoza being a starter, the Raiders' offensive line only allowed 11 sacks when Kirk Cousins was quarterback. Last Sunday, with the 2026 NFL Draft's top pick under center, they gave up six to the Seahawks. If Denver wants to win the game, their defensive front seven has to dominate. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph needs to throw everything he can at the rookie signal caller and rattle him early and often. — Christopher Hart Keep feeding Jonah Coleman I don't need to discuss numbers. Just look at how much better the offense is when Coleman gets his touches. Whether he's running the ball or catching passes, he gives the offense a weapon that forces the defense to respect what Denver is doing in the trenches, thus opening up the opportunities for Bo Nix to push the ball downfield. — Adam Malnati Blow a team out for once I know, I know. It's just not how this team is built. Every team gets a chance to beat the Broncos, but most of them fail to do so in the final minutes. Buuuuut, it would sure be nice to enjoy a good ol' fashioned butt-whoopin' type game — especially against the Raiders. — Tim Lynch Score more points than the Raiders The Broncos scored more points than the Panthers a few weeks ago and didn't need to score any last week, because they were on a bye. Now, it's Raiders week, and my key to the game is simple. Score more points than the Raiders. Denver is 7-0 when it does that and 0-2 when it does not. Using advanced analytics, I say the Broncos have a 100% chance to win on Sunday if they score more points than the Raiders. That is my key to the game! — Scotty Payne What are your keys to Sunday's game?

Las Vegas has lost two straight while Denver has reeled off five straight wins. This will be Mendoza’s first start on the road, and it comes against one of the more ferocious and stingy defenses in the NFL. Denver’s defense is allowing only 20.7 points per game. Their pass rush has produced 26 sacks, with Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen at 4.5 apiece. Last week the Raiders surrendered six sacks. Speaking of last week, Las Vegas is coming off a 21-13 home loss to the defending champion Seattle Seahawks, a game in which Mendoza showed promise early in his first NFL start before the Raiders’ offense faded. He completed 11 of 13 passes for 90 yards in the first half and scored on a 10-yard run but finished just 17-of-29 for 143 yards as Seattle’s pressure took over and sacked him six times. Even more damaging was the loss of star tight end Brock Bowers , who injured his ankle and played only 11 snaps. His status is questionable for this weekend and is certainly worth monitoring. away.headline: Brock Bowers returns to practice ahead of Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 11 matchup against Denver Broncos
away.blurb: The Raiders’ leading receiver exited last week’s game against the Seattle Seahawks at halftime and missed Wednesday’s session with ankle and quadricep injuries. This was a step in the right direction for Bowers’ availability on Sunday against the Broncos, as the Raiders listed him as limited on the injury report (h/t The Athletic’s Sam Warren ). Also, Las Vegas’ offense really needs its top target. Additionally, Warren noted that guard Trey Zuhn III (illness), defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (stinger) and defensive tackle Foley Fatukasi (toe) weren’t spotted during the media viewing period of Thursday’s practice. Zuhn wasn’t listed on Wednesday’s report, while Hemingway was a non-participant and Fatukasi was limited on Wednesday. Neither of the three linemen participated in Thursday’s session. Warren also reported that the Raiders brought in kickers Lucas Havrisik, Younghoe Koo and John Parker Romo for a workout, as Matt Gay is dealing with a hip injury and sat out of practice. Tight end Ian Thomas added an ankle injury to Thursday’s report after missing Wednesday with a calf injury, though Thomas was upgraded to limited on Thursday. As for the Broncos, they managed to get healthier for the second practice of the week. The only changes from yesterday’s injury report were cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle), defensive tackle Zach Allen (rest) and wide receiver Courtland Sutton (rest) going from limited to full participants. The Las Vegas Raiders received good news ahead of their Week 11 matchup against the Denver Broncos . ESPN’s Ryan McFadden posted a video of tight end Brock Bowers in full pads and participating in warmups ahead of Thursday’s practice, noting that Bowers is returning to the field. The ‘tight end’ has racked up 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns in eight games this season, leading the Silver and Black in all three categories despite missing the first two contests with a knee injury. According to Sumer Sports , the team’s passing game averages 0.105 EPA per pass and has a 49.0 percent success rate with Bowers on the field this year. Without him, those numbers dip to 0.005 EPA per pass and 43.4 percent. Factor in that rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will be making his second career start against a Denver defense that ranks ninth in points per game allowed ( 20.7 ), and it’s even more important that Bowers suits up on Sunday. If Zuhn can’t go, second-year guard Caleb Rogers is likely the next man up. Rogers replaced Zuhn when the latter left the 49ers game with a concussion a couple of weeks ago. Hemingway’s and Fatukasi’s absence would really test the Raiders’ defensive tackle depth, a position that’s been an issue all season. That would likely mean more reps for Adam Butler, Tim Keenan III, Thomas Booker IV and JJ Pegues.

away.headline: Report: Raiders TE Brock Bowers avoids major ankle injury
away.blurb: The team initially listed him as questionable to return and he came back in the second quarter with his right ankle heavily taped. He made one catch before returning to the locker room and ultimately being ruled out. Bowers, 23, finished the 21-13 defeat with two receptions for 18 yards. The third-year pro out of Georgia raised his team-leading season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards with six touchdowns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Bowers is day-to-day. "It's not as bad as we thought but still a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak said. Bowers, a two-time Pro Bowl selection, was hurt while blocking on a running play during the Raiders' opening drive. Multiple players rolled up on the back of his leg as he was making the block. A first-round pick (13th overall) by Las Vegas in 2024, Bowers has accumulated 226 receptions for 2,550 yards and 18 touchdowns in 37 career games (32 starts). He was a first-team All-Pro as a rookie. This story was originally published November 16, 2026 at 10:59 AM . away.headline: Raiders dealt considerable injury disadvantage with Broncos coming off their bye
away.blurb: After a physical game against the Seattle Seahawks last Sunday, the Raiders are dealing with a few bumps and bruises; nothing out of the ordinary. But the Broncos are coming off their bye, so they practically have a clean bill of health heading into this heated divisional matchup. Concussions can often keep a player out for one game, but because Denver had its bye week, both players were able to make a full recovery. And that's a good thing, because head and neck health is important, but it certainly does not help Las Vegas' chances of winning in Week 11. Matt Gay being a bit banged up is not great, either. He has been lights-out as a kicker this year, and with the ball moving differently at a mile above sea level on Sunday, Las Vegas needs him to be at the top of his game. Hip injuries can be worrisome for a kicker, depending on the hip, of course. With the Broncos not having any injury concerns this week, fresh off their bye, it hurts to have Bowers potentially out and another starter at least banged up. But the Raiders haven't done well playing against injured teams this year, so maybe they'll thrive with the shoe on the other foot. Not even close to everything has gone right for the Las Vegas Raiders during the 2026 NFL season. But one benefit that they've carried in their back pocket throughout the campaign has been relatively good health , which has given them an edge in seemingly every single game. Have the Silver and Black always taken advantage of that edge? No. But in several contests, they have gotten to face skeleton crews with a fully staffed roster. That is changing this week, though, with the AFC West rival Denver Broncos on the schedule for Week 11. All year, Las Vegas has been at an advantage in the injury department. Now, they're up against it. Broncos' injury report is as thin as it gets before clash with Raiders Both teams released their injury reports after Wednesday's practice. Here is how things went in Denver: Nobody is wishing injury on the Broncos, but of course, as fate would have it, they get a handful of key players back when they face the Raiders. Jaylen Waddle and Riley Moss, both of whom suffered concussions in Week 9, are back at practice with no limitations and will play on Sunday. Talanoa Hufanga is also back this week, it seems, after missing four straight games for the Broncos' secondary. He was playing well before suffering an ankle injury, and he missed an entire month. But with an extra week off to prepare, he will re-emerge against the Raiders, of course. Caleb Loehner is also back this week after beginning the season on IR. He is a promising young tight end prospect that, if you can believe anything that Sean Payton says, has a bright future in Denver. The Broncos have been looking for a spark at tight end, so he could be involved right away. away.headline: Raiders vs. Seahawks Week 10: Expert predictions, storylines, injuries and more
away.blurb: After a two-game road stretch, the Raiders will return home in Week 10 as they welcome the Seattle Seahawks to Allegiant Stadium. Sunday's game will be on CBS, not FOX, as it was the last two weeks. And getting Ian Eagle and Ross Tucker on the broadcast is tremendous for those watching at home. Las Vegas is remarkably healthy for this juncture in the season, or really any point in the NFL calendar. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams will not suit up, which is an act of god for the Silver and Black, and starting left tackle and guard Charles Cross and Quenton Nelson are out, too. It still won't be easy against a talented Seattle skill position group, as Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Zach Charbonnet and others pose legitimate threats . But with Drew Lock under center and two elite offensive linemen who would protect his blind side out due to injury, Las Vegas has a chance. home.headline: Brock Bowers returns to practice ahead of Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 11 matchup against Denver Broncos
home.blurb: The Raiders’ leading receiver exited last week’s game against the Seattle Seahawks at halftime and missed Wednesday’s session with ankle and quadricep injuries. This was a step in the right direction for Bowers’ availability on Sunday against the Broncos, as the Raiders listed him as limited on the injury report (h/t The Athletic’s Sam Warren ). Also, Las Vegas’ offense really needs its top target. Additionally, Warren noted that guard Trey Zuhn III (illness), defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (stinger) and defensive tackle Foley Fatukasi (toe) weren’t spotted during the media viewing period of Thursday’s practice. Zuhn wasn’t listed on Wednesday’s report, while Hemingway was a non-participant and Fatukasi was limited on Wednesday. Neither of the three linemen participated in Thursday’s session. Warren also reported that the Raiders brought in kickers Lucas Havrisik, Younghoe Koo and John Parker Romo for a workout, as Matt Gay is dealing with a hip injury and sat out of practice. Tight end Ian Thomas added an ankle injury to Thursday’s report after missing Wednesday with a calf injury, though Thomas was upgraded to limited on Thursday. As for the Broncos, they managed to get healthier for the second practice of the week. The only changes from yesterday’s injury report were cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle), defensive tackle Zach Allen (rest) and wide receiver Courtland Sutton (rest) going from limited to full participants. The Las Vegas Raiders received good news ahead of their Week 11 matchup against the Denver Broncos . ESPN’s Ryan McFadden posted a video of tight end Brock Bowers in full pads and participating in warmups ahead of Thursday’s practice, noting that Bowers is returning to the field. The ‘tight end’ has racked up 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns in eight games this season, leading the Silver and Black in all three categories despite missing the first two contests with a knee injury. According to Sumer Sports , the team’s passing game averages 0.105 EPA per pass and has a 49.0 percent success rate with Bowers on the field this year. Without him, those numbers dip to 0.005 EPA per pass and 43.4 percent. Factor in that rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will be making his second career start against a Denver defense that ranks ninth in points per game allowed ( 20.7 ), and it’s even more important that Bowers suits up on Sunday. If Zuhn can’t go, second-year guard Caleb Rogers is likely the next man up. Rogers replaced Zuhn when the latter left the 49ers game with a concussion a couple of weeks ago. Hemingway’s and Fatukasi’s absence would really test the Raiders’ defensive tackle depth, a position that’s been an issue all season. That would likely mean more reps for Adam Butler, Tim Keenan III, Thomas Booker IV and JJ Pegues.

home.headline: Raiders dealt considerable injury disadvantage with Broncos coming off their bye
home.blurb: After a physical game against the Seattle Seahawks last Sunday, the Raiders are dealing with a few bumps and bruises; nothing out of the ordinary. But the Broncos are coming off their bye, so they practically have a clean bill of health heading into this heated divisional matchup. Concussions can often keep a player out for one game, but because Denver had its bye week, both players were able to make a full recovery. And that's a good thing, because head and neck health is important, but it certainly does not help Las Vegas' chances of winning in Week 11. Matt Gay being a bit banged up is not great, either. He has been lights-out as a kicker this year, and with the ball moving differently at a mile above sea level on Sunday, Las Vegas needs him to be at the top of his game. Hip injuries can be worrisome for a kicker, depending on the hip, of course. With the Broncos not having any injury concerns this week, fresh off their bye, it hurts to have Bowers potentially out and another starter at least banged up. But the Raiders haven't done well playing against injured teams this year, so maybe they'll thrive with the shoe on the other foot. Not even close to everything has gone right for the Las Vegas Raiders during the 2026 NFL season. But one benefit that they've carried in their back pocket throughout the campaign has been relatively good health , which has given them an edge in seemingly every single game. Have the Silver and Black always taken advantage of that edge? No. But in several contests, they have gotten to face skeleton crews with a fully staffed roster. That is changing this week, though, with the AFC West rival Denver Broncos on the schedule for Week 11. All year, Las Vegas has been at an advantage in the injury department. Now, they're up against it. Broncos' injury report is as thin as it gets before clash with Raiders Both teams released their injury reports after Wednesday's practice. Here is how things went in Denver: Nobody is wishing injury on the Broncos, but of course, as fate would have it, they get a handful of key players back when they face the Raiders. Jaylen Waddle and Riley Moss, both of whom suffered concussions in Week 9, are back at practice with no limitations and will play on Sunday. Talanoa Hufanga is also back this week, it seems, after missing four straight games for the Broncos' secondary. He was playing well before suffering an ankle injury, and he missed an entire month. But with an extra week off to prepare, he will re-emerge against the Raiders, of course. Caleb Loehner is also back this week after beginning the season on IR. He is a promising young tight end prospect that, if you can believe anything that Sean Payton says, has a bright future in Denver. The Broncos have been looking for a spark at tight end, so he could be involved right away. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars-Giants: Bhayshul Tuten's Field Day Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are set to take on the New York Giants in one of Week 11's most interesting matchups, and there is plenty at stake for both teams. For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best. So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions. Bhayshul Tuten Hits 100 Yards Rushing No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)." Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks. Jaguars Limit Giants to Under 3.5 YPC The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game. With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut. Parker Washington Makes Another 50+ Yard Catch No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab. According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.." The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver. Jaguars Force 3 J.J. McCarthy Turnovers J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that. The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week. Jessie Bates III Plays Every Snap Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for. McCarthy, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the Jacksonville Jaguars, this is a big one. The Jaguars are set to face their toughest test since the bye week ended with the 5-3-1 New York Giants in Week 11. A game that head coach Liam Coen has already said will have to be won in the trenches will be a challenge the Jaguars haven't faced in Weeks. To preview the Jaguars and Giants clash as Jacksonville prepares for their second-half playoff run, we spoke with Patricia Traina of Giants OnSI to go behind the scenes and get an idea of what the Jaguars can really expect. So, how does Traina see this game from the Giants' perspective, and what will it take for Jacksonville to win? We break it down below. 1) What is Arvell Reese more dangerous at: playing linebacker or rushing the passer? Traina: Both. Overall, Reese ranks third among Giants linebackers (inside and outside) with 14 pressures per NFL+, and he has the second-lowest average time to sack (4.0 seconds) in that group. And the scary thing is that this young man, whose name has been mentioned for Defensive Rookie of the Year honors, is just getting started. Reese as a pass rusher (just 107 times so far) as he has been in coverage (246 times). I would think that as the game continues to slow down for him, he will see an increase in his role. 2) How do you view the matchup between Malik Nabers and Travis Hunter? Traina: I think that’s going to be a key matchup. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy has done a good job of scheming Nabers open this season by moving him around the formation. When playing in the slot, he has an 84.6% reception rate and has scored both of his touchdowns from the slot. Travis Hunter hasn’t worked much from the slot this season. They have Hunter down as having played six total snaps in the slot, defending just one target that was not completed. I am very interested in seeing how much the Giants put Nabers in the slot on Sunday and, when he’s not in the slot, how much, if any, the Jaguars have Hunter travel with him. 3) How much have the Giants trusted J.J. McCarthy when it comes to attacking defenses downfield? Explosive plays have been one of the Jaguars’ few weaknesses. Traina: Overall, the Giants have a 44.7% passing completion rate (10th in the league) on deep balls of 20+ air yards. This season, McCarthy has a 52.6% completion rate on deep passes of 20+ air yards. As you might guess, Nabers has been the main target on those deep balls., he’s caught 12 of 21 (57.1%) with one drop. Rookie Malachi Fields has caught three of nine, and Darnell Mooney one of six. Tight end Isaiah Likely has caught three of seven deep passes. As I’m guessing the Jaguars will do everything possible to take Nabers out of the equation, I suspect this could be a good opportunity for Fields to have a breakout game. 4) What kind of impact has former Jaguars CB Greg Newsome made in New York? Traina: He’s been outstanding in coverage, so much so that the Giants recently gave him a three-year contract extension. He currently has a career-best 71.2 coverage grade from PFF and has allowed opponents just a 57.6% completion rate. Newsome has also allowed just 61 YAC, has yet to surrender a touchdown, and has five pass breakups, all good for a 63.8 NFL coverage rating, which is the best of his career. 5) If Jacksonville wins this game, what do you think would be the biggest reason why? They make the Giants one-dimensional. The Jaguars have one of the best run defenses in the league right now, and I’m fairly certain they’ll zero in on shutting down running back Cam Skattebo and challenging McCarthy to beat them through the air. McCarthy is 9-4 as a starter in games where his offense has rushed for 100+ yards collectively. That’s not to say McCarthy and the Giants can’t pull off the upset, but if they become one-dimensional, it’ll be that much harder for them to do so. As my readers and listeners have reminded me, the Giants ran up a storm against the Houston Texans a few weeks back, posting a season-high 188 yards against a Texans run defense that was top five going into that game. So yes, the Giants have a chance. Published 15 hours ago JOHN SHIPLEY John Shipley has been covering the Jacksonville Jaguars as a beat reporter and publisher of Jaguar Report since 2019. The Jaguars don’t have their cornerbacks following receivers, but this might be the week to consider it. As for the Jaguars’ offense vs. the Giants’ defense, I am going with Walker Little against Abdul Carter. Little has played well for the Jaguars since stepping in as the starting left tackle a month ago due to injuries, but a player on Carter’s level hasn’t tested him. Little has proven he can get the job done week in and week out, but this week will be about proving that he can handle playing a blue-chip talent, which is exactly what he will need to do during a critical playoff run. Q: What’s the most underrated part/player of the Jaguars’ overall plan of attack? Jacksonville Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect JS: Anthony Campanile. The Jaguars’ defensive coordinator is a genius, turning one of the NFL’s worst defenses into a powerhouse over the last two years. JS: Anthony Campanile. The Jaguars’ defensive coordinator is a genius, turning one of the NFL’s worst defenses into a powerhouse over the last two years. They are not flawless, since they still give up some explosive plays, and they do not get a ton of sacks. But Campanile has built one of the best run defenses in the NFL, and his philosophy of forcing quarterbacks to get the ball out of their hands quickly has led to plenty of takeaways and big plays. Campanile should be a future head coach, and the proof is in the pudding: he has helped elevate and evolve the Jaguars’ defense over the past two years. Q: The Jags have been blowing out opponents. What are your expectations for this week, though? Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect JS: I don’t think the Jaguars have a blowout this week, even though I believe they are firmly the better team. JS: I don’t think the Jaguars have a blowout this week, even though I believe they are firmly the better team. The Giants have fought hard week in and week out under John Harbaugh, and I think there is a real chance they take the fight to the Jaguars in the trenches. I think Trevor Lawrence will still be taking snaps in the fourth quarter this week, which has not been a given most weeks. There is a lot more respect in the Jaguars’ building right now than there was the last time these two teams played in 2022. Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants face major test this week when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars. It is also a game that will provide a huge swing in the Giants' expected chances to make the playoffs. Will the Giants upset Jacksonville? See what our Big Blue View staff members think about that game and the rest of the Week 11 action in this week's staff picks. I don't think the Giants win this game. I think there's a path to a win for the Giants, if they can find it. The Giants are one of the very best teams in the NFL at forcing drives to end in punts. At the same time, the Jaguars will be without their starting center and the Giants are one of the best teams in the League at creating quick pressure. That's important because Trevor Lawrence has been one of the quarterbacks most affected by pressure in the NFL. At the same time, the Giants have rediscovered the explosive pass with J.J. McCarthy, which has been the weakness of the Jags' defense. If the Giants can score touchdowns while disrupting Lawrence, they've got the chance to come away with the upset. We've seen the Giants rebound after bad games, as well as play much better than anticipated when they're underdogs. Maybe both will happen here. The flip side of the coin is simpler and scarier to me: The Giants have one of the worst red zone defenses in the NFL, and the Jaguars have one of the best red zone offenses in the league. If the Giants can't stop them between the 20s, this game could get ugly fast. Pick: Jaguars Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the league with a young and explosive offense that can run the football. Their defense is aggressive but doesn't NEED to bring the blitz — they blitz at about a league-average rate, but Anthony Campanile does an excellent job utilizing simulated pressure to harass opposing quarterbacks. Jacksonville is third in offensive EPA, 4th in defensive EPA allowed, and 1st in Net EPA — they're a juggernaut based on their performance and the advanced analytics. Still, that doesn't mean the Giants don't have a chance — they just must play efficient football and avoid the catastrophic mistakes that have robbed them of wins. It's possible, but against the most efficient team in the NFL, it will be difficult. John Harbaugh will have the Giants ready and prepared for the game, and I believe it will be more exciting and competitive. Jacksonville is concluding their third straight road game, which could give the Giants a slight advantage at home, but I ultimately believe the better team finds a way to win. David Hartman It took 11 weeks, but for the first time this season, the Giants will face a team with a winning record when the 7-2 Jaguars come to town on Sunday. Not only is Jacksonville running away with the AFC South (they lead the division by four games), but they're steamrolling the competition. They've won their last three games by a combined 75 points. This is easily Big Blue's toughest test of the season, so far. Jacksonville is very good on both sides of the ball. They're fourth in offensive DVOA, third in defensive DVOA, and third in overall DVOA. They also have an excellent field goal kicker with crazy range. If you look at both rosters, it's hard to find clear advantages for the Giants at any position group outside of tight end, and even there, Jacksonville has good players. Can the Giants win this game? Yes. They're at home, they're getting an extra three days of rest, and as we saw when they played Houston, they aren't scared and can surprise as a big underdog. They'll need to dial it up on defense and pressure Trevor Lawrence into the kinds of mistakes he used to make before Liam Coen got there. They also might have a little extra motivation after letting last week's game against the Commanders slip away at the end. I won't be surprised if John Harbaugh's team hangs in there and keeps it as a one-score game most of the way. But in the end, until the Giants show me that they can beat a really good team, I can't pick them to do so. Tony Del Genio You can talk yourself into believing that the Giants can beat Jacksonville this Sunday. They needed a miraculous last-second 57-yard field goal to beat the Eagles team (with Jalen Hurts) that the Giants defeated (without Hurts). They lost to the Texans team that the Giants beat the following week. The woeful Titans were within a TD against them last week with 5 minutes left. So indeed, it could be a competitive game. Unfortunately, the Jags have also won games by 24, 29, 35, and 23 points this season. They have scored 31 or more in each of their past four games, and over 40 in two of those. The Giants have only scored more than 30 points once, and only then because of a 99-yard pick-6 on the last play of the game. Trevor Lawrence isn't necessarily playing any better this year than in the past. He's a QB that simultaneously makes great passes and puts the ball up for grabs, yet unlike in years past, he's cut down on the INTs while getting the TDs. Part of that may be due to 5'10" wide receiver Parker Washington (a 2023 6th-round pick), who had a breakout 2025 and is on pace for 1,000 yards. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, a 4th round 2025 pick, isn't quite in the Jahmyr Gibbs – Kenneth Walker class but he's not far below and is a missed tackle machine. A lot of the credit has to go to head coach Liam Coen, who also calls the plays and turned this team around as soon as he was hired. Lawrence, like most QBs, has trouble with pressure, but he is not too fazed by the blitz. Finding a way to disrupt his rhythm is a key to any chance the Giants may have. On defense, the Jaguars are strong at linebacker with fourth-round 2023 pick Ventrell Miller, one of the league's best (note how many mid-round picks the Jags have hit on), along with Foyesade Oluokun. They also put on a decent pass rush with Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, and Dennis Gardeck. In the secondary, Travis Hunter is playing more like a No. 2 pick, having mostly given up his evening gig as a receiver. Are the Giants a serious playoff contender? This is the type of game they can use to make a statement against a team that is in the Super Bowl conversation. I think they'll put up a fight. I also don't think they're there yet. Pick : Jaguars Valentine's View I want to convince myself to pick the Giants to defeat the Jaguars. I really do. I just can't. The Jaguars are a team with justifiable Super Bowl ambitions . They are a well-rounded team with a high-powered offense, a very good defense, and one of the best field-goal kickers in the business in Cam Little. The Giants are a good team. They are resilient. They will give the Jaguars their best shot. Maybe, just maybe, it will be good enough to pull off an upset that would go a long way toward ensuring that the Giants make the playoffs. I just can't pick them to do it.

Teams like the Chicago Bears , Buffalo Bills , Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos — you know, the contenders in this league right now — are all matched up with teams well out of the playoff race. Throw in the fact that six teams are on bye, and the schedule gets leaner. But we do have two big-time matchups with the Jacksonville Jaguars visiting the New York Giants and then a huge Sunday Night Football showdown in Mexico City with the Minnesota Vikings taking on the San Francisco 49ers for NFC supremacy. But regardless of the quality of matchup, we have every game covered in our NFL picks and predictions. We're coming off of two winning weeks in a row and are getting our mojo back. Surely a week in which there are numerous double-digit spreads with heavy and deserved favorites won't come back to haunt us. But here we go, once again delivering with NFL picks for Week 11 with predictions for every game straight-up and against the spread. Toughest NFL Week 11 prediction to make Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Minnesota Vikings (+3) vs. San Francisco 49ers – in Mexico City Minnesota Vikings (+3) vs. San Francisco 49ers – in Mexico City Point blank, these are two of the three best teams in the NFC right now. So you throw in the fact that this game is at a neutral site in primetime and it makes it even more difficult. Looking at these two teams, though, people are going to look at the 49ers and their high-powered offense and be intrigued by that. But the Vikings have proven that, under Brian Flores, they're capable of slowing down anyone. Heck, the Lions and Packers both found that out — even if the Detroit got the win thanks to Kyler Murray. But now Kirk Cousins is back in the fold for Minnesota and we've seen him already step in and raise the baseline of the Vikings offense substantially. Who knew getting Justin Jefferson the ball was the smart play? It's that end of the field that ended up being my deciding factor here, though. The fact that the Vikings offense has found this new level of competency complements the defense so incredibly well. Moreover, the 49ers defense, though talented, hasn't exactly been infallible of late. So in Mexico City, give me the Vikings staying hot and establishing a foothold in the NFC. Easiest NFL Week 11 pick on the board Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III, quarterback Caleb Williams | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5) New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5) This feels scarily too easy. Like, have oddsmakers watched the Saints recently? This defense is struggling mightily right now and the offense isn't exactly lighting the world on fire anymore either. To add to that, the Bears have been clinical more often than not this season (the last time out against the Buccaneers where Caleb Williams couldn't stop throwing picks, notwithstanding). Now we get Ben Johnson and this team coming out of a bye where they've had time to gameplan and get healthier. Yeah, that's all lining up pretty heavily toward Chicago for me, especially with this game being played in the Windy City. It's not that I think this game will end up being just a mauling on the Bears' part (though that's also not out of the question). The Saints should be able to score a bit. But it feels like Chicago will just have more consistent and perhaps unstopped success that will ultimately allow them to pull away handily. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6.5) at Detroit Lions Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6.5) at Detroit Lions Yes, I'm aware that Baker Mayfield's health is (once again) in question coming into this game. That's not me saying I have full faith in Jalon Daniels getting back into the offense, though he didn't play that poorly when he had to step in earlier in the season. What I think people are overlooking in this matchup is the fact that the Lions are coming off of the win in Munich and now have to travel back across the country and not get a bye week between games. That has happened for eight teams this season, traveling back from Europe and playing again in one week, and those teams are 2-5-1 straight-up, much less against the spread favored by more than a touchdowns. When you then factor in losing Aidan Hutchinson last week and what that could mean for Detroit's defense — which I wasn't exactly over the moon about to begin with — there's a path here for the Bucs to keep this close. I'll still take the Lions to win straight-up, mainly because I'm a coward and understand they are the substantially better team in this matchup. away.blurb: The Jaguars dropped their initial injury report for week 11. Center Robert Hainsey was a non-participant. This doesn't come as a surprise when you take into account that head coach Liam Coen had already stated that the veteran hog molly won't be available against New York. With Hainsey expected to sit out the Giants game, Jonah Monheim will get the starting nod at center. It will be the first time the former USC Trojan starts a game this season. On the other hand, running back Bhayshul Tuten popped up on the injury report. He has been dealing with ankle and foot injuries. Mia O'Brien of ESPN Radio noted on Twitter that the sophomore out of Virginia Tech showed up to practice without his helmet . Apart from Tuten, safety Antonio Johnson (ankle), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (ankle), defensive tackle Matt Dickerson (neck), running back Chris Rodriguez (hand), linebacker Jalen McLeod (groin), defensive end Travon Walker (rib), defensive end Danny Striggow (concussion), and Monheim (ankle) were listed as limited participants. Robert Hainsey is questionable for Jaguars vs. Titans, Bhayshul Tuten good to go The Jacksonville Jaguars are 7-2 for the first time since 1999 after winning three games in a row. While nobody will deny that they have dominated, the teams the Jags defeated weren't very good. That will change in Week 11, when they face the New York Giants. The G-Men aren't necessarily a juggernaut, but at 5-3-1, they're nothing to scoff at. They currently lead the NFC East and are the kind of club Jacksonville cannot afford to take lightly. Compounding the issue is that the Jaguars' injury report for Week 11 is quite long. Robert Hainsey and Arik Armstead didn't practice Wednesday Hainsey was dealing with a concussion but cleared protocol ahead of the AFC Showdown against the Tennessee Titans. He started the game but left with a knee injury. Although the injury isn't season-ending, he'll be week-to-week , according to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN. Aside from Hainsey, defensive tackle Arik Armstead didn't participate, but it was due to personal reasons. He should be back either Thursday or Friday. Tuten hasn't missed a game in spite of the injuries. He toted the rock a season-high 26 times for 88 yards against Tennessee. He'll probably miss Thursday's practice again to keep recovering. away.headline: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus
away.blurb: The Jaguars had 11 players carry either a limited or did-not-participate designation into Thursday's practice. Some names, like center Robert Hainsey's DNP situation due to a knee injury, were expected. But there was one change to Thursday's injury report that will trump all other names: Bhayshul Tuten, who was downgraded to a non-participant in practice after practicing in a limited fashion on Wednesday, which now creates quite the injury development to monitor before the Jaguars play the New York Giants in Week 11 on Sunday afternoon. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen has said in recent days that he has been pleased with Tuten's performances and toughness over the last two weeks. Add this to the fact that he played the last few weeks without a full week of practice, and it is hard to imagine Tuten sitting this one out, even if his injury will now come even more into focus. The Jaguars also had the following players listed as limited on Thursday: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- We are at that point of the season where injury reports closer resemble CVS receipts, and the Jaguars' Thursday injury report certainly checks that box. Tuten's status is a key one to watch any week, but especially in Week 11 when the Jaguars' running game is supposed to be pivotal against a blitz-happy Giants front that will test the Jaguars in the trenches. Tuten has played in each of the last two games despite practicing just once in those two weeks, and the Jaguars clearly did not feel like Tuten couldn't handle the bulk of the carries when he got 26 carries against the Titans on Sunday. “Obviously, last year being in a supplemental role, and I thought he was tough last year in some of the runs that he had where he just would kind of get whacked pretty good, get up and continue to play," Coen said on Wednesday. "To carry the load that he took this past week with 26 carries and play the amount of snaps he played still not quite 100%. I think the guy is probably mentally and physically tougher than I would've maybe imagined in ways." The smart bet would be to prepare for Tuten to play, but that does not mean this will not be a situation to monitor. It is such a key injury to watch in large part because the Jaguars have leaned on Tuten significantly over the course of the season. The second-year running back is arguably one of the three most important players on the offense alongside Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington, and he has vastly outproduced the rest of the Jaguars' running back room. This is a big one, just like each game is a big one. But unless something changes on Friday, Tuten still should be considered a key part of Sunday's game.
